newsitem.title: UK: OMI hopes to sign deal with MTL this month.
newsitem.headline: OMI hopes to sign deal with MTL this month.

text.p: OMI Corp, a U.S. tanker owner, said on Tuesday it hoped to sign a definitive deal to acquire privately-owned Marine Transport Lines (MTL) by the end of August.
Completion of the deal, which is a key plank in OMI's corporate restructuring, remains unlikely before the first quarter of next year due to tax and legal considerations.
Vincent de Sostoa, OMI chief financial officer, told Reuters: "We are looking to complete the signing of documents with MTL by the end of this month."
He said OMI would file details of the agreement with U.S. tax authorities shortly after.
Sostoa added: "This is a very complex transaction. There are complex legal issues and complex tax issues. We still expect to be on track to complete in the first quarter 98."
OMI announced in June that it had reached agreement in principle to merge with MTL.
The all-paper deal will see OMI spin off its U.S. trading assets to MTL, allowing OMI to move its domicile offshore and outside U.S. tax regulation.
A key element in the deal will be the U.S. tax authorities view of OMI's deferred tax liabilities, shipping analysts said.
OMI is also considering moving its corporate headquarters from New York to Houston in order to cut costs.
Sostoa said OMI's second quarter results, announced late Monday, were in line with the company's expectations.
"It was a planned quarter," he said. "There were a set number of vessel dry-dockings, and the markets were strong largely as expected."
OMI reported net income of $1.278 million in the three months to the end of June, up from $675,000 in the same period a year earlier, despite revenues falling to $55.6 million from $61.3 million.
OMI has withdrawn from a number of tanker owning joint ventures, sold a number of older vessels, and refinanced its debt.

The company plans to concentrate on two market sectors: suezmax crude tankers, of which it has four newbuilding contracts, and handysize petroleum product carriers. -- Reuters Shipping Desk +44 171 542 4087/4012. Fax 5017
